discovery: Discovery of topological and geometric phases in quantum mechanics (the Aharonov-Bohm effect and the Berry phase)

nominees.name: Yakir Aharonov
nominees.affiliation: Chapman University, USA, and Tel Aviv University, Israel

motivation: Aharonov (with the late David Bohm, 1959) showed that electromagnetic potentials have direct physical effects: charged particles acquire a measurable phase when they encircle a flux they never touch. Berry (1984) showed that any quantum system carried slowly around a closed loop in parameter space acquires a geometric phase set only by the path's geometry. These started as questions many physicists thought meaningless, and together they changed how we understand the quantum wavefunction. Both have been confirmed decisively, the Aharonov-Bohm effect in Tonomura's electron holography. Geometric phases now run through physics: topological insulators, the quantum Hall effect, polarization optics, molecular dynamics, anomalous transport and holonomic quantum computation. The 2016 prize for topological phases rested on this foundation. Aharonov's later work on weak values also created a new experimental approach to quantum measurement. Recognizing this discovery would honour foundational insight whose reach across physics is exceptional.
